submissions.findingTextShort: A randomized-trial meta-analysis found a small depressive-symptom signal with DHEA, but GRADE certainty was very low.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 32930419 / DOI 10.1002/jnr.24721 synthesized randomized DHEA trials across depression and other clinical populations. A small pooled depressive-symptom improvement was reported, but GRADE certainty was very low and sensitivity analyses showed influential studies affected heterogeneity. This supports only tentative indication-specific language, not a general mood, stress, or anti-aging recommendation.
submissions.populationContext: Mixed psychiatric and medical populations with depressive symptoms across randomized trials.
submissions.usageContext: DHEA regimens and endocrine contexts varied across trials.
submissions.safetyContext: Androgenic adverse effects were reported; endocrine conversion remains relevant to safety.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Very-low-certainty evidence and heterogeneous populations prevent high-confidence efficacy claims.

submissions.findingTextShort: Pooled randomized-trial data show DHEA effects on hormones, bone density and body composition are sex-specific rather than generic anti-aging effects.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 30421439 / DOI 10.1111/cen.13901 pooled four randomized trials in adults age 55 years and older. DHEA changed downstream androgen/estrogen exposure differently in women and men, and BMD/body-composition responses were not uniform across sex or skeletal site. The result constrains generic anti-aging, bone-health and body-composition claims and makes downstream hormonal conversion central to interpretation.
submissions.populationContext: Older women and men enrolled in four similar randomized DHEA trials.
submissions.usageContext: Daily oral DHEA in older adults; sex and baseline endocrine context materially affect interpretation.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Surrogate and body-composition outcomes do not establish broad clinical-outcome benefit.

submissions.findingTextShort: In elderly men, DHEA showed no clear benefit across several clinical outcomes; a small fat-mass effect was explained by downstream sex-hormone conversion.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 23824417 / DOI 10.1210/jc.2013-1358 meta-analyzed 25 placebo-controlled trials involving 1,353 elderly men. A small fat-mass reduction lost significance after adjustment for DHEA-derived testosterone and estradiol changes, while lipid/glycemic measures, bone health, sexual function and quality of life showed no clear benefit. These nulls directly constrain broad male anti-aging claims.
submissions.populationContext: Elderly men in double-blind placebo-controlled DHEA trials.
submissions.usageContext: Oral DHEA supplementation with mean follow-up around 36 weeks across included studies.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Outcome-specific nulls and endocrine mediation must remain first-class rather than being collapsed into a positive body-composition claim.

submissions.findingTextShort: A randomized-trial meta-analysis found no clear change in total cholesterol, LDL-C or triglycerides but a modest HDL-C reduction, especially in women.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 32675010 / DOI 10.1016/j.numecd.2020.05.015 synthesized 23 randomized-trial articles. Total cholesterol, LDL-C and triglycerides were not significantly changed overall, while HDL-C decreased modestly; the HDL reduction was significant in studies comprising women but not men. This is a metabolic safety counterweight and does not establish cardiovascular-event harm or a universal sex-specific effect outside the included trials.
submissions.populationContext: Adults across randomized DHEA supplementation trials; sex-stratified analyses were reported.
submissions.usageContext: DHEA doses and durations varied across trials.
submissions.safetyContext: HDL-C is a surrogate marker; major adverse cardiovascular outcomes were not established by this analysis.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Do not convert a biomarker shift into a proven cardiovascular-risk outcome or universal dose threshold.

submissions.findingTextShort: A randomized-trial meta-analysis found no significant pooled AST or ALT change, but that biomarker null is not proof of comprehensive or long-term liver safety.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 34342920 / DOI 10.1111/ijcp.14698 found no statistically significant pooled change in AST or ALT across the included randomized DHEA trial arms. The paper's broad liver-safety conclusion exceeds what transaminase nulls alone can establish: the analysis does not prove absence of rare idiosyncratic injury, long-term harm, product-quality effects, or safety in unstudied endocrine-risk populations. Preserve the null biomarker result without upgrading it into universal liver-safety reassurance.
submissions.populationContext: Participants across randomized DHEA supplementation trials included in the meta-analysis.
submissions.usageContext: DHEA regimens varied; pooled AST/ALT outcomes only.
submissions.safetyContext: Normal pooled transaminase effects are narrower than comprehensive hepatotoxicity assessment.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Rare-event, duration, product-quality and population-transfer limits remain unresolved.
